How to Submit Public Comment:
Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City Clerk
prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the Chair’ s
discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the Community Services
Commission.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website as noted below. Public
Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the Commission
before the meeting for their consideration but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted
after 4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Commission but may not be received before the meeting.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

Watch the Meeting Online

   MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 3, 2025
 REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Barrantes called the regular meeting of the Community Services Commission to order at
6:34 P.M. on Monday, November 5, 2025, with Commissioners and staff in the Council Chamber
at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vice Chair Rodriguez.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Cheryl Cabot, Davis Barrantes, Nancy Duong, Mary
  Huang, Darwin Rodriguez

Commissioners Absent:  None

ANNOUNCEMENTS
Assistant Director Morales-Stevens provided information for the public on how to submit
comments and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the Community Services
Commission, email all public comments to CSCommission@sgch.org.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  The Agenda Order was approved by the Commission.

2. PUBLIC COMMENT

  None.

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  NOVEMBER 3, 2025
 3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A motion was made by Commissioner Cabot and seconded by Vice Chair Rodriguez
  to approve the minutes of the Community Services Commission Meeting for October
  6, 2025.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 5-0-0- as follows:

  AYES:  BARRANTES, CABOT, DUONG, HUANG, RODRIGUEZ
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. EVENTS AND PROGRAMS UPDATES
  Presented by Assistant Director Morales-Stevens.

  Pamela Scott and Starr Anger were introduced to the Commission and warmly
  welcomed.

  The Commission suggested hosting events outside the Mission District, they feel this
  would make it more accessible for more San Gabriel neighborhoods. Commissioners
  recommended increasing advertising for the Mini Mashed Potato Dash and sending
  a survey for feedback on the new Turkey Trot location.

  Regarding the Fall Fun Festival, they enjoyed the event and inquired about
  coordinating with schools holding trunk-or-treat events on the same night. They
  requested food trucks display prices more prominently and suggested reaching out
  to new vendors.

  The Commission discussed Taste of San Gabriel, they mentioned restaurants might
  not be able to provide free food, and one commissioner suggested reconsidering the
  event.

  B. DISCUSSION OF WORKPLAN
  Presented by Chair Barrantes.

  The Commission expressed interest in hosting a bike event at either Marshall Park or
  Vincent Lugo Park. They inquired about sponsors for our special events and suggested
  the possibility of organizing an event at 99 Ranch or TAWA Supermarket.

  Public Comment: None
COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  NOVEMBER 3, 2025
 5. COMMISSIONER REPORTS

  Commissioner Cabot attended the Fall Fun Festival and served as a judge for the costume
  contest. She shared that there’s a new art studio in town, Artists & Makers.

  Commissioner Duong attended an event by Assembly Mike Fong. She shared information
  regarding California commissions and boards and available seats.

  Chair Barrantes and Vice-Chair Rodriguez attended the Fall Fun Festival.

6. STAFF COMMENTS

  Assistant Director Morales-Stevens shared information regarding Veterans Ceremony.

7. ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Barrantes adjourned the meeting at 8:19 p.m.

  The next regular meeting held on Monday, December 1, 2025, in the Council Chamber at
  City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776, at 6:30 pm.

SUBJECT:  Community Services Commission Resident Survey

The Community Services Commission has actively sought responses to the Commission
Resident Survey, since 2023 to determine individuals’ familiarity with the department.

Below are the lists of questions the Vice Chair Rodriguez has prepared for the new
engagement survey with minor edits provided by Assistant Director Morales-Stevens.

  Valley Blvd.?

  3. How often do you visit City of San Gabriel parks and facilities?

  o Once a month

  community activities and events?

As a reminder, the survey would be uploaded to Survey Monkey and distributed digitally
via email social media and the website, and in person at events. The Commissioners are
encouraged to assist with the in-person collection efforts.

At the last regular meeting the commission determined that the purpose of the survey is
to determine how aware the participant is of the programs, events and services offered
within the City.

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  November 3, 2025

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Assistant Director

SUBJECT:  Community Services Commission Workplan

SUMMARY
The Community Services Commission approved the most recent workplan at the October
7, 2024 commission meeting the Community Services Commission decided to change it
from an annual workplan to an ongoing document that can be adjusted if and when
needed to better address the needs of the department. The Commission will conduct a
comprehensive evaluation of the workplan every six months to determine if major
changes need to be made. At the July and October 2025 Commission meetings the
Commission provided edits to staff, which are included in this report.

PURPOSE OF THE COMMISSION
The purpose of the Community Services Commission is to creatively and inclusively
explore ways in which the Community Services Department can enrich quality of life for
residents of the City of San Gabriel by providing equitable access to dynamic programs,
services and spaces that strengthen community connection and engagement.

SCOPE OF THE COMMISSION
The Community Services Commission serves as an advisory body to the Community
Services Department and City Council, and functions as a liaison between residents and
city government. It is the responsibility of the Community Services Commission to
advocate on behalf of the San Gabriel community and to ensure that the Community
Services Department’s programs, services, spaces and events advance the Commission’s
purpose.

Purpose of the Workplan
The Annual Workplan is intended to guide the work of the Community Services
Commission and outline the areas of focus for 2024. It includes proposed programs and
projects that will be implemented and completed throughout the year.
 Current Workplan
The workplan sets four priority areas as identified in the Community Services
Strategic Plan for the Community Services Department. The following list of ideas,
programs and activities are not intended to be exhaustive or to limit the action items the
Commission can explore. The list below reflects amendments made at the July and
October Regular Community Services Commission Meetings.

  1. Create New Innovative Programs and Services to Engage the Entire
  Community
  a. Provide programs for residents with the age groups, 13-18 and 30-50.
  b. Explore program offerings for persons with disabilities including but not
  limited to swim classes.
  c. Continue the youth ambassador program for the Community Services
  Commission
  i. Appoint two ambassadors
  d. Optimizing participation- Gaining residents vs non-residents

  2. Connect the Entire Community to Enhance Quality of Life
  a. Connect all geographic areas of the City
  i. Examples include: Hosting events and programs in the South San
  Gabriel area and various other neighborhoods such as a tiny tots
  soccer class at Marshall Park or a partnership with the Garvey School
  District.
  ii. Introduction of contract class soccer lessons at Marshall Park
  b. Host a bike/ sustainable transportation event at Marshall Park
  i. Partners could include Active SGV, Metro, PD Bike Safety
  ii. Highlight RideSG service
  c. Host resource fair at Marshall Park.

  3. Develop Innovative Resources and Tools to Achieve our Mission
  a. Modify resident survey and collect data with targeted questions to improve,
